podcast.title: First Creation Records Release
podcast.body: The Legend was the artist responsible for the very first release from Creation Records, which came out in the summer of 1983. "The first release came from an artist called The Legend in the summer of 1983..."

xref.title: Bill Barilko and the "50-Mission Cap"
xref.body: The "Fully Completely" album features a song referencing the legend of Bill Barilko's plane crash and the Stanley Cup curse on the Toronto Maple Leafs, bizarrely mentioning a "50-mission cap." This cap, a baseball-type worn by WWII fighter pilots, symbolized a seasoned pilot who had survived at least 50 missions. In the song, Downie uses it as a metaphor for people, like his character, who feign experience by distressing their cap, much like he admits to quoting a hockey card (specifically card #340 from the 1991 NHL Pro Set Hockey Cards about Barilko) to appear more knowledgeable. "Barilco's story is just a metaphor for the image Gord's character in the song wanted to portray."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music

xref.title: Growing Posthumous Legend
xref.body: Following their initial breakup, The Velvet Underground's reputation and musical legacy experienced a resurgence, with critics hailing them as massive musical pioneers and hundreds of bands acknowledging them through name-checking or covering their material. "The legend and the rep of the velvet underground took on a life of its own. Several generations of musicians and music fans began to recognize the velvet's important musical legacy."

xref.title: Name Change to The Stooges
xref.body: Shortly after their debut as Iggy and the Psychedelic Stooges, the band's name was shortened to simply "The Stooges," marking the beginning of the legend of Iggy Pop. "The psychedelic studios soon became just the stooages. And here begins the legend of Iggy Pop."

xref.title: Posthumous Popularity Surge
xref.body: After Kurt Cobain's death, the band experienced a significant "spike in popularity and sales" that has continued to the present day, with albums, books, and box sets remaining strong sellers. "But after he died and the myth and the legend was secured, Nirvana experienced a spike in popularity and sales that continues to, while the present day, the albums continue to sell the books, the box set, the whole works."

xref.title: Stephen Patrick Morrissey's Fanaticism
xref.body: The legend of the New York Dolls grew to "mythic proportions," captivating Stephen Patrick Morrissey (singer for The Smiths) from a young age, who wrote letters to British music magazines praising them and founded their British fan club. "One of their biggest all-time fans was Stephen Patrick Morrissey. Yes, the same guy who sang for the Smiths."
